subject: The live model turn loop -- Odyssey promotion gate G4's central requirement
why_this_gate_mattered: Everything HIDE had wired before this was upstream of the thing that actually produces tokens. The archaeology found HIDE_MODEL_WEIGHTS required for any generation, so the turn loop had never been exercised end to end against a served model. G4 states outright that a stub provider returning canned text fails the gate -- the entire archaeology exists because things looked wired and were not.
live_path_claimed: SubmitTurn intent -> context compile -> RuntimeSupervisor/HttpModelProvider -> canonical SSE model events -> streamed TokenBatch -> persisted agent.message -> next turn rebuild_history sees it
why_the_claim_is_credible_before_i_re_ru: The test is a real integration test (crates/hide-backend/tests/live_model_turn.rs, 524 lines) that stands up a serve process and drives the live intent path, not a unit test on an inner function.
It runs against a real Llama GGUF discovered from the HF cache or HIDE_MODEL_WEIGHTS -- there is no canned provider in the path.
It asserts the round trip completes AND that the next turn's rebuild_history sees the persisted message, which a stub could not fake without also faking persistence.
Runtime ~148s, consistent with real generation rather than a mock.
honest_caveats: This is a bounded Qwen-0.5B functional integration run, not a large-model TG or production-GPU certification.
The run did not collect a CLEAN lease or artifact-bound GPU timestamp receipt, so it cannot certify production performance.

The test skips cleanly when no weights are present or HIDE_LIVE_MODEL_TURN=0. A passing CI run alone is insufficient; the executed command and non-empty live output below are the authority for this revalidation.
